items.title: “That’s one grown-up doing three jobs …”
items.where: The inner child, the guards, and the inner adult’s three jobs, P2
items.my_version: Here I’m going to talk about what you develop in yourself as you reparent your inner child. I’m going to talk about it in terms of three jobs: your loving Nurturer, your safe Adult Protector (hereafter just the Protector) and your wise Guide. That’s one grown-up doing three jobs, not three more people moving in to help with the rent, and each job keeps the others in balance. It’s you that needs to develop these qualities.

items.title: “That way you keep the good parts of feeling younger …”
items.where: Let the child speak without handing over the steering wheel, P3
items.your_version:
Let the child speak while you define the goal

Your inner child wants to be heard, but they don't want to feel like they have to steer the ship while they're in the emotional storm. By providing this protective healing guidance for them, you gain access all of the positive aspects of what it can be like to as free as an unburdened child. All the wonder, silliness, approaching things through the senses more, feeling it’s ok to be vulnerable, to want someone to take care of you, to feel need without the stigma of "needy," and to want to offload some decision making, while your adult part stays present. At the same time you get to leave behind the difficulties that came with really being a kid: having to obey, not being able to do much for yourself, getting scolded, and not understanding how things work yet.

"It is okay for a younger part of me to talk.  I understand that the adult in me is always going to be here, listening, evaluating, protecting me and stopping me if needed. I'm not handing my adult decisions over to a younger part of me, or to a hypnotist or a recording, or to anyone else."

items.title: “That takes warmth, and if there isn’t any yet, borrow some.”
items.where: Love doesn’t have to wait for trust, P3
items.my_version: Then respond to the complaints that are sure to come. You don't have to accept every conclusion they reach about you, but do listen for the concrete complaint without fighting the yelling and swearing around it, because even if they are coming from a place that is not completely "right," there will likely be something true in what they are saying. If it's something serious, answer it seriously. Do what you can to show your love for them. This might include some or all of the following: Learning to listen to them when they are angry without hitting back. Owning what was not okay. Working on changing yourself so that you are less likely to turn on them. Finding other ways to make up to them for what you did. Finding other ways to show your love for them (this might include taking care of them, such as by buying and cooking food for them, setting limits for them, taking them to the doctor when they need it, and doing what you said you would do). Just not hitting back is enough to start being the adult, even if it isn't enough yet for them to trust you. Even that takes some warmth, and if you don't have any yet, borrow some from someone who's been good to you, or from an adult you imagine.

items.title: “No warmth today? …”
items.where: The two-hand practice, P3
items.my_version: Begin to send love from your heart down to your inner child and just notice what comes up for you. If some comes back up, let it, and send it on down again, so it goes around like a loop. That part's a gift from them, and they don't owe it to you, so if nothing comes back, just keep sending yours. If you feel resistance, just meet it with love. If you feel or see something, just meet that with love as well. If you can't find any warmth today, just leave your hands where they are and notice what's there. Don't pretend to feel something you don't. Let it go back and forth between your heart and your inner child, like a real conversation.

items.title: “… ask it what it’s trying to stop, or what it wants.”
items.where: Working with your guards, P3
items.my_version:
Instead, you might feel numb, cynical, angry, suddenly hungry, like you need to look at your phone, sexually aroused, like you need to make plans, sleepy, dissociated, or you might even think that what you're doing is stupid. Those are not failures. Often what you're experiencing is a very charming guard. It's what protects you when your consciously installed parental Protector isn't functioning, the same as when you were a child. It might not be a guard at all, though. Maybe it's your inner child, mad that you took so long to come back. Maybe it's your inherited parent script, or something from earlier today, or a bit of each. So before you decide where it's coming from, ask it what it's trying to stop, or what it wants.

Talk to the guard the way your Nurturer talks to your inner child: “I see you. I'm not going to force my way past you. What's going on?” Then wait and listen patiently. If nothing comes back, that's okay, you don't need to push for an answer. Later on, you can ask it, “What are you afraid would happen if you stopped protecting me by…?”

items.title: “Can you pause before you act? …”
items.where: Don’t rush the repair, P5
items.your_version:
Don’t rush the repair
When your inner child does show up, spend some quality time with them before taking off the kid gloves, so to speak, and jumping into the healing work. 
They might like to hear something like, “Little one, I’m here with you now. You don’t have to work to explain anything. I'm not asking you to impress me with how fast you can get better. Can I help you feel less alone?”
What does your inner child need? It can be anything: warmth, to play, to be protected, to mourn, to be angry, food, rest, boundaries, better relationships, to stop fantasizing, to stop working their butt off, that you keep a promise to them today, etc. etc.
When a younger you, a guard, a feeling or a signal comes up in your body, take it slowly:
A. Prepare yourself to tend to them with some privacy, but still able to access support if needed. Check how much grown-up you is really in the room first. Can you take a moment before you react? When you decide something, do you follow through? If you answered "No," because right now you’re mostly still stuck identifying as the frightened little boo, hold off on the deeper conversation. Do what makes you feel adult before you try to talk to little you.

items.title: “If being still tends to make you sleepy …”
items.where: Make the hypnosis more alert, P1
items.your_version:
Once you’ve got your bearings, make your first wish.

"Please show me the next truth. The next symbol or feeling. The question or action that's useful for me at this time, and no more than I can handle."

Stay awake when your mind likes to escape

If your mind keeps drifting off, sit up and open your eyes. Then feel your feet on the floor, and just let your breathing go at its own pace. Tell yourself, "I'm not going anywhere. I'm happily arriving more fully here each moment."

Pick something in the room to look at, and feel your spine  at the same time (focusing on two things makes it harder for the mind to use multitasking mode to wander). Then ask yourself what the daydreaming is doing for you. Is it bringing you guidance? Does it help you work through a feeling, or are you using it to avoid something?

Ask for any diffuse benefits to become more practically focused: "If this is guidance, show me what I need to do about it. If I'm avoiding something, bring me gently back to the present and show me what it is."

Make the hypnosis more alert

Aside from focusing on things in your direct experience, you can also suggest yourself into greater alertness (it's still relaxed-alert, not paranoid-alert). Keep your eyes open. items.title: “If your recording cuts out partway through …”
items.where: Come all the way back, P5
items.your_version:
If your recording happens to cut out partway through, woops... you could end up lying there dazed & confused, waiting on a voice that isn't coming back. Don't worry, you don't have to be a vegetable forever. Just tell yourself, "The recording has stopped and we're all done now. Welcome back to me!" (that exclamation actually helps, because trance is kinda monotone). Then do the exit-trance count and the present-time checks above on your own. Once your eyes are open, "touch grass" as they say, for grounding. Or if no grass, just push your adorable feet or hands into something solid. The physical feeling connects your brain to your body.
Sleep recordings are another story, since you're assuming you'll drift off midway with those. But if the sleep recording is designed to also wake you back up, make sure it's doing so intelligently, not just using a vague exit word that might half wake up and still leave you a bit blank or "under the spell" so to speak.

items.title: “We’re going back to the life we’re building.”
items.where: Finish without forcing a revelation, P1
items.your_version: Don’t feel that you have to end the session with a great revelation (those are often flaky, not standing the test of time). When you have done as much as you want to do, ask yourself what would help you leave things where they are for now. This might include thanking parts for their help, or making sure that you do something in real life (put a boundary in place, get some rest, repair a relationship, keep a promise etc). You can tell your little one, "That’s enough for today, choochoo. Aren't you excited to get back to the life we're building?"

items.title: “Once or twice a week …”
items.where: The weekly deeper practice, P1
items.your_version:
Once or twice a week, when it’s useful, give this practice more space and time so even the unplanned, unknown and maybe hidden needs can show up. Just because it's unplanned doesn't mean it will be more shocking. Start from your Higher Self, from the field of acceptance and understanding, or however you can describe it that makes it feel accessible. If you need the Protector or another of your adult jobs, bring it in or borrow it from someone safe. Mr. or Ms. Protector can check to make sure you’re not skipping past anything important. Leave enough time at the end to come all the way back up & out.
Then, if there's something from the session that asked you to do something in real life, and your Protector agrees, then go ahead and do it when you can. That's how you show your subconscious you mean business.

items.my_version:
Bridge words, like ‘as’, ‘whilst’, ‘because’, ‘when’, ‘after’, ‘before’ and ‘which means’, link one event to the next, so the first can seem to come with the second, or even cause it. That doesn't mean it does, of course.

Lots of hypnotists use them to claim too much, like: “Because I breathe, the trauma leaves.”
items.before:
Bridge words are words like ‘as, whilst, because, when, after, before, which means’ etc. These are words that link events, which can make something seem like it goes along with or produces the next thing. That doesn't mean it actually does, of course.

Here's an example of some of the overly commanding bridge language many hypnotists will use: “Because I breathe, the trauma leaves.”

items.title: “As an example, I won’t tell anyone to override their fear …”
items.where: What I will not use NLP for, P4
items.your_version:
What I will not use NLP for
Here is a list of things I don't do with NLP, whether I'm hypnotizing myself or someone else:
I don't use NLP to convince anyone an intuition is true. For example, I don't use NLP or hypnosis in general, to do more than initial memory retrieval work. Memories retrieved still need external validation, especially when they were led to (which NLP tends to).
On the other hand, I also don't use NLP to talk anyone out of a real signal. That doesn't mean we can't try to calm unbearable pain, but we must keep access to the awareness of the signal so that we can do the real root cause healing.
For example, I won’t tell anyone to push past their fear before asking what it’s protecting, and I won’t make anyone feel rushed when they want time to take to process the feelings.

items.title: “Gently change an aspect of your pattern’s representation …”
items.where: Running the whole NLP sequence, P6
items.your_version:
Running the whole NLP sequence
Here is a rough outline of the entire NLP process:

Induce yourself (meaning gather your attention into a soft focus) or contain yourself (meaning stabilize yourself) first if you are already too opened up to difficult memories/experiences.

Ask yourself for permission: is it useful to work with this pattern today?

Get a representation of your pattern. Do you see it as an image, with size, color and location, or do you feel it like a movement or some other kind of sensation?

Find out if that part/pattern is protecting something for you.

Gently change an aspect of your pattern's representation from the prior step.

Bring in your three good adults. The Nurturer to brings love in. Next, the Protector puts your helmet on, and then the Guide points the way out of the mess. They’re really all one inner adult, but picturing each with their own function can be easier before merging them together (like Captain Planet if you saw that cartoon).

Then anchor the good state you're in with a hand on your heart, two fingers touching, a particular breath or a posture, so that doing the same thing later can bring the state back.

Imagine running into a scenario where your old pattern would have triggered, and adopt a feasible new behavior. ("If I see a red cloth, then I will choose not to charge at it. I am not a bull anymore.")

Check in with your body for signals during the re-imagining process, and what else besides body signals supports your new interpretation of the situation. Ask yourself whether the new behavior you've imagined is kind and sensible.

Then come all the way back out of the altered state (see “Come all the way back”), and go do something normal.

items.title: Hypnosis-specific audit
items.where: Hypnosis-specific audit, P1
items.your_version:
Before you let a hypnotic recording or a live hypnotist put suggestions into your head, interview them a bit, so you don't get manipulated.

First, what are they going to do to bring you under? And if you react to something, will they pause or change the script, or stop and bring you all the way back?

(cut: Can my responses lead to pausing or modifying the script, …)

Then, if you can't tell what's going on, do they take that as proof the process worked? Are they using identity roles, obedience ladders, age regression, or your wish to belong, to get past your adult judgment?

(cut: Is the hypnotist using identity roles, obedience ladders, age regressions, …)

Keep in mind though, you can only answer that last one by reading the script first, or by telling them what your adult judgment would accept, since they can't be expected to know that.

Will they tell you before they use fractionation, cues, or anything else that affects your memory or what you do after the session?

Are they quietly turning what you feel in your body into evidence for something they'd already decided?

And when it's time to come out, will they tell you clearly that the session is over, so you get your normal waking (and walking) self back and can think critically again?

If any answer is unclear, be careful. Ask for the exact script. If they don't want to give it, change the method, or walk right out that door.

items.before:
Before accepting a hypnotic recording or live suggestion, ask these important questions to avoid being manipulated:

What induction mechanics are being used to bring me under the spell?

Can my responses lead to pausing or modifying the script, or stopping & coming to full alertness?

Does the hypnotist treat my lack of awareness of what's going on as some kind of proof that the process worked?

Is the hypnotist using identity roles, obedience ladders, age regressions, or desires for/assumptions of belonging to lower my adult self's better judgment?

Keep in mind though, the answer to that last one requires either checking the script first, or explaining what your adult judgement would accept, as the hypnotist can't be expected to know that.

Are fractionation, cues, or other methods of affecting my memory or modifying my post-session behavior disclosed before they are used?

Is the hypnotist implicitly turning my bodily sensations into evidence for a prior assumption?

When we're ready to exit hypnosis, will they give me a clear statement that the session has ended, and would I get back my normal waking (and walking) identity? Will I be able to use my critical judgement abilities as before?

When any answer to these questions is unclear, beware. Ask for the exact script. If they don't want to give it, change the method, or walk right out that door.

items.title: “Then you’re allowed to stop holding yourself hostage …”
items.where: Forgiving yourself, P2
items.your_version:
Forgiveness without bypass

We cannot force forgiveness on ourselves. It has to come from a place of understanding, otherwise it can be bypassing. However, if we remain in the anger forever, we are allowing the injury to dictate how we live our lives in the present. So how do we hold all of this? We just remember that it can all be true at once. They really did hurt us and they still have to answer for it. Our boundary with them is crucial to maintain, especially after forgiveness which can tend to weaken it. One day we may find that we have forgiven them for not knowing better, just like Jesus did on the Cross.

You might say to the part of you that got hurt, “I’m not going to use spiritual mumbo jumbo to shush your cries and make you forgive before you're ready. But I’m also not going to build our whole life around this wound forever.”


Forgiving yourself

For self-forgiveness, name what you regret doing, and take responsibility for just that part. Let yourself feel the remorse by taking in the harm done. See how it went against your values. Stop short of making yourself a permanent criminal by identifying with the behaviors you're now abandoning.

Do what you can to put it right. Every so often, come back to how you got to be someone who could do that, until you understand the pattern well enough that it can't drive you anymore.

items.title: “Now keep your sense of agency during the answer phase.”
items.where: 9. No-trance inner contact, P4
items.your_version:
No-trance inner contact

We don't need to go into trance to get a lot of the benefits of the communion technique! Here's my no-trance version:

For pacing (warm-up), notice reality as it is now. What do you see around you? Is today Monday, your favorite day of the week? Hopefully your name didn't suddenly change to Larry.

For the suggestion: in your mind, ask a clear question and then listen gently.

Now keep your sense of agency during the answer phase. You might notice an answer popped up, or you might decide you don't know. You can always take a break or rephrase the question. Sometimes you might ask advice from someone else.

Keep aware of the subtle inner signal: write whatever you get. It might be a word or sensation. An impulse or objection. Sometimes there's no signal, just silence, itself a kind of signal. Don't jump to interpreting it as validation of some theory.

Hand off the role: have your adult self answer that same question in whatever way is appropriate, preferably by writing or doing.

Integration/exit: reality test the signal you noticed. As part of testing, if it seems appropriate, you can do something simple based on it.

There's no elaborate exit protocol here since you didn't go into trance. Just close the exercise and carry on with your day.
